1.q: נִדְרַ֨שְׁתִּי֙ לְ⁠ל֣וֹא שָׁאָ֔לוּ נִמְצֵ֖אתִי לְ⁠לֹ֣א בִקְשֻׁ֑⁠נִי אָמַ֨רְתִּי֙ הִנֵּ֣⁠נִי הִנֵּ֔⁠נִי אֶל־גּ֖וֹי לֹֽא־קֹרָ֥א בִ⁠שְׁמִֽ⁠י
1.note: See how your translation team has decided to represent pairs of clauses in Hebrew poetry that mean basically the same thing. Alternate translation: [“I was ready to respond to people who did not even ask for me. I said ‘Behold me! Behold me!’ to a nation, it was not called by my name.]

The expression **I was sought** is a passive verbal form. If it would be unnatural to use that form, you could express the idea in active form or in another way that is natural in your language. Alternate translation: [Those who did not ask sought me]

The expression **I was found** is a passive verbal form. If it would be unnatural to use that form, you could express the idea in active form or in another way that is natural in your language. Alternate translation: [they who did not seek me found me]

1.q: אָמַ֨רְתִּי֙ הִנֵּ֣⁠נִי הִנֵּ֔⁠נִי אֶל־גּ֖וֹי לֹֽא־קֹרָ֥א בִ⁠שְׁמִֽ⁠י
1.note: If it would be clearer in your language, you could translate this so that there is not a quotation within a quotation. Alternate translation: [I urgently told a nation that was not called by my name to behold me]

The expression **it was not called by my name** is a passive verbal form. If it would be unnatural to use that form, you could express the idea in active form or in another way that is natural in your language. Alternate translation: [that did not call upon my name]

Yahweh is using **it was not called by my name** as a common expression of the culture to mean “they did not belong to me.” If this phrase does not have that meaning for your readers, you could use a comparable expression from your language that does have that meaning, or you could state the meaning plainly. Alternate translation: [that did not belong to me]

2.note: Spreading out the hands was a symbolic action by which Yahweh showed that he was appealing to the people and inviting them to return to him. If it would be helpful to your readers, you could explain the significance of this action in the text of your translation or in a footnote. Alternate translation: [I spread out my hands in appeal all of the day]

In this verse, the word **people** is singular in form, but it refers to all the Israelites as a group. If it would be helpful in your language, you could use the plural form of “people.” Alternate translation: [a group of rebellious persons]

Here Yahweh is speaking as if the way the people were living were **a way** that they were **walking** along. Your language may have a comparable expression that you can use in your translation, or you could state the meaning plainly. Alternate translation: [ones who behave wickedly]

3.note: Here, **to my face** represents “in my presence.” If it would be helpful in your language, you could use an equivalent expression or plain language. Alternate translation: [in my presence]

Yahweh assumes that the Israelites will know that making altars from **bricks** was a sacrilege because he had commanded them to make altars only from unhewn stones. The implication is that the people were burning this incense as part of worshiping false gods rather than Yahweh. You could include this information if that would be helpful to your readers. Alternate translation: [to false gods on bricks]

4.note: The implication is that the people did these things in order to consult the spirits of dead people. You could include this information if that would be helpful to your readers. Alternate translation: [sitting among graves and lodging in secret places in order to consult the spirits of dead people]

5.q: קְרַ֣ב אֵלֶ֔י⁠ךָ אַל תִּגַּשׁ בִּ֖⁠י כִּ֣י קְדַשְׁתִּ֑י⁠ךָ
5.note: If it would be clearer in your language, you could translate this so that there is not a quotation within a quotation. Alternate translation: [telling others to keep to themselves and not come near them, because they are holier than others]

5.q: אֵ֚לֶּה עָשָׁ֣ן בְּ⁠אַפִּ֔⁠י אֵ֥שׁ יֹקֶ֖דֶת כָּל הַ⁠יּֽוֹם
5.note: Here Yahweh is speaking of these people as if they were **smoke** in his nose and **a fire burning all of the day**. He means that they constantly irritated and provoked him. Your language may have a comparable expression that you can use in your translation, or you could state the meaning plainly. Alternate translation: [These people constantly irritated and provoked me all day long]
The pronoun **These** refers to the rebellious people whom Yahweh has been describing in the previous verses. It may be helpful to clarify this for your readers. Alternate translation: [These people]

6.note: Isaiah is using the term **Behold** to focus his listeners’ attention on what he is about to say. Your language may have a comparable expression that you can use in your translation. Alternate translation: [Look]

The expression **it is written** is a passive verbal form. If it would be unnatural to use that form, you could express the idea in active form or in another way that is natural in your language. Alternate translation: [I have written it]
See how you translated the similar expression in 65:3.

Yahweh is using **into their lap** as a common expression of the culture to mean “paying them back fully.” If this phrase does not have that meaning for your readers, you could use a comparable expression from your language that does have that meaning, or you could state the meaning plainly. Alternate translation: [and I will pay them back fully]

7.note: If your language does not use an abstract noun for the idea of **iniquities**, you could express the same idea in another way. Alternate translation: [the wrong things you have done and the wrong things your fathers have done]

In the previous verses, Yahweh referred to these people in the third person, but here he shifts to addressing them directly in the second person with the words **your iniquities and the iniquities of your fathers**. If it would be helpful in your language, you could refer to the people in the same person that you use in the surrounding verses. Alternate translation: [their iniquities and the iniquities of their fathers]

The word **your** is plural in both instances because Yahweh is addressing rebellious Israelites as a group. The words “you” and “your” in verses 11-15 are plural for the same reason. So use the plural form in your translation if your language marks that distinction.

Here Yahweh is speaking as if the people’s ancestors were their **fathers**. Your language may have a comparable expression that you can use in your translation, or you could state the meaning plainly. Alternate translation: [and the iniquities of your forefathers]

7.q: קִטְּרוּ֙ עַל הֶ֣⁠הָרִ֔ים וְ⁠עַל הַ⁠גְּבָע֖וֹת חֵרְפ֑וּ⁠נִי
7.note: The implication is that the people burned this incense to idols at pagan worship sites on the mountains and hills. You could include this information if that would be helpful to your readers. Alternate translation: [they have burned incense to idols at pagan worship sites on the mountains and have provoked me on the hills]

8.q: כַּ⁠אֲשֶׁ֨ר יִמָּצֵ֤א הַ⁠תִּירוֹשׁ֙ בָּֽ⁠אֶשְׁכּ֔וֹל וְ⁠אָמַר֙ אַל תַּשְׁחִיתֵ֔⁠הוּ כִּ֥י בְרָכָ֖ה בּ֑⁠וֹ כֵּ֤ן אֶֽעֱשֶׂה֙ לְמַ֣עַן עֲבָדַ֔⁠י
8.note: The point of this comparison is that just as good **juice** that **is found in a cluster** of grapes is worth preserving, so Yahweh considers his **servants** worth preserving. If it would be helpful in your language, you could make this point explicitly. Alternate translation: [Just as good juice found in a cluster of grapes is worth preserving, so, because my servants are worth preserving to me, I will act on their behalf]

The expression **is found** is a passive verbal form. If it would be unnatural to use that form, you could express the idea in active form or in another way that is natural in your language. Alternate translation: [one finds juice in a cluster]
If it would be clearer in your language, you could translate this so that there is not a quotation within a quotation. Alternate translation: [not to destroy it, because a blessing is in it]

9.note: Here Yahweh is speaking of the descendants of Jacob as if they were **seed** that Jacob produced. Your language may have a comparable expression that you can use in your translation, or you could state the meaning plainly. Alternate translation: [descendants from Jacob]

The pronoun **it** refers to the land of Yahweh’s mountains, mentioned earlier in the verse. It may be helpful to clarify this for your readers. Alternate translation: [and my chosen ones will possess my mountains]

10.q: וְ⁠הָיָ֤ה הַ⁠שָּׁרוֹן֙ לִ⁠נְוֵה צֹ֔אן וְ⁠עֵ֥מֶק עָכ֖וֹר לְ⁠רֵ֣בֶץ בָּקָ֑ר
10.note: Yahweh is referring to all of the land by naming two of its regions, **Sharon** in the west and **the Valley of Achor** in the east. If it would be helpful in your language, you could use an equivalent expression or plain language. Alternate translation: [And all the land will be a pasture for the flock and a resting place for the herd]

Yahweh is leaving out some of the words that in many languages a sentence would need in order to be complete. You can supply these words from the context if that would be clearer in your language. Alternate translation: [and the Valley of Achor will be for a lying down of the herd]

11.note: If your language does not use an abstract noun for the idea of **holiness**, you could express the same idea in another way. Alternate translation: [my holy mountain]

Here, **the mountain of my holiness** represents Mount Zion, the place where Yahweh’s temple stood. If it would be helpful in your language, you could use an equivalent expression or plain language. Alternate translation: [Mount Zion, my sacred mountain]

11.q: הַֽ⁠עֹרְכִ֤ים לַ⁠גַּד֙ שֻׁלְחָ֔ן וְ⁠הַֽ⁠מְמַלְאִ֖ים לַ⁠מְנִ֥י מִמְסָֽךְ
11.note: The words **Fortune** and **Destiny** are the names of two false gods.

12.note: Here, **for the sword** represents being killed violently. If it would be helpful in your language, you could use an equivalent expression or plain language. Alternate translation: [to be killed violently]

Here Yahweh is speaking of the people being killed as if they were animals that would **bow down to the slaughter**. Your language may have a comparable expression that you can use in your translation, or you could state the meaning plainly. Alternate translation: [will die in the slaughter]

Yahweh is using **in my eyes** as a common expression of the culture to mean “in my judgment.” If this phrase does not have that meaning for your readers, you could use a comparable expression from your language that does have that meaning, or you could state the meaning plainly. Alternate translation: [in my judgment]

13.note: The word **Therefore** indicates that what follows is a result of what Yahweh said before it. Use a connector in your language that makes it clear that what follows is a result of what came before. Alternate translation: [Because you did those things]

13.q: הִנֵּ֨ה עֲבָדַ֤⁠י יֹאכֵ֨לוּ֙ וְ⁠אַתֶּ֣ם תִּרְעָ֔בוּ הִנֵּ֧ה עֲבָדַ֛⁠י & יִשְׁתּ֖וּ וְ⁠אַתֶּ֣ם & תִּצְמָ֑אוּ הִנֵּ֧ה עֲבָדַ֛⁠י & יִשְׂמָ֖חוּ וְ⁠אַתֶּ֥ם & תֵּבֹֽשׁוּ
13.note: The pronoun **you** is stated separately here even though the verbs translated as **you will hunger**, **you will thirst**, and **you will have shame** already include this meaning. Yahweh is doing that in each of these three statements to emphasize the contrast between what will happen to his servants and what will happen to the people he is addressing. If a speaker of your language would use an explicit pronoun for the same purpose, you may want to use that construction in your translation. If not, your language may have other ways of showing the meaning here. Alternate translation: [Behold, my servants will eat, but as for you, you will surely hunger. Behold, my servants will drink, but as for you, you will surely thirst. Behold, my servants will rejoice, but as for you, you will surely be ashamed]

13.q: הִנֵּ֨ה עֲבָדַ֤⁠י יֹאכֵ֨לוּ֙ וְ⁠אַתֶּ֣ם תִּרְעָ֔בוּ הִנֵּ֧ה עֲבָדַ֛⁠י & יִשְׁתּ֖וּ וְ⁠אַתֶּ֣ם & תִּצְמָ֑אוּ הִנֵּ֧ה עֲבָדַ֛⁠י & יִשְׂמָ֖חוּ וְ⁠אַתֶּ֥ם & תֵּבֹֽשׁוּ
13.note: These three clauses mean basically the same thing. The second and third emphasize the meaning of the first by repeating the same idea with different words. If it would be helpful to your readers, you could combine them and express the emphasis in another way. Another approach would be to connect the phrases with a word that shows that the second phrase is repeating the first one, not saying something additional. See how you as a team have decided to translate the parallel phrases in poetry, and follow that approach here and throughout this chapter. Alternate translation: [Behold, I will give my servants plenty to eat and drink and reason to rejoice, but you will suffer hunger, thirst, and shame]
If your language does not use an abstract noun for the idea of **shame**, you could express the same idea in another way. Alternate translation: [you will be ashamed]

Yahweh uses the term **Behold** three times to focus his listeners’ attention on what he is about to say. Your language may have a comparable expression that you can use in your translation. Alternate translation: [Hear me]

14.note: Isaiah is using the possessive form to describe a **heart** that is characterized by **goodness**. If a speaker of your language would not use the possessive form for this, you could express this idea in another way. Alternate translation: [because their hearts are glad]

Here the **heart** represents where a person’s feelings exist. You may have a comparable expression in your language, or you could state the meaning plainly. Alternate translation: [because of their good feelings]
Here, **breaking of spirit** represents deep despair. If it would be helpful in your language, you could use an equivalent expression or plain language. Alternate translation: [and from deep despair]

15.note: Yahweh is using **you will leave your name as a curse** as a common expression of the culture to mean that people will use their name as an example when they call down a curse on someone. If this phrase does not have that meaning for your readers, you could use a comparable expression from your language that does have that meaning, or you could state the meaning plainly. Alternate translation: [And your name will become a word for a curse]

16.note: If your language does not use an abstract noun for the idea of **truth**, you could express the same idea in another way. Alternate translation: [by the God who is true]

The expression **will be forgotten** is a passive verbal form. If it would be unnatural to use that form, you could express the idea in active form or in another way that is natural in your language. Alternate translation: [people will forget the former troubles]

The expression **will also be hidden** is a passive verbal form. If it would be unnatural to use that form, you could express the idea in active form or in another way that is natural in your language. Alternate translation: [for I will also hide them]

Here, **my eyes** represent Yahweh’s attention. If it would be helpful in your language, you could use an equivalent expression or plain language. Alternate translation: [they will also be hidden from my attention]

17.note: Yahweh is referring to all of creation by naming its two major components, **new heavens** and **a new earth**. If it would be helpful in your language, you could use an equivalent expression or plain language. Alternate translation: [a completely new world]

The expression **behold me** is one that people of this culture would commonly use to mean that they were about to do something. If it would be helpful in your language, you could state the meaning plainly. Alternate translation: [I am about to create]

The expression **will not be remembered** is a passive verbal form. If it would be unnatural to use that form, you could express the idea in active form or in another way that is natural in your language. Alternate translation: [and no one will remember the former things]

Yahweh is using **come up upon the heart** as a common expression of the culture to mean “come to mind.” If this phrase does not have that meaning for your readers, you could use a comparable expression from your language that does have that meaning, or you could state the meaning plainly. Alternate translation: [they will not come to mind]

18.note: The terms **rejoice** and **be glad** mean similar things. Yahweh is using the two terms together for emphasis. If it would be clearer for your readers, you could express the emphasis with a single phrase. Alternate translation: [be very glad]

The expression **behold me** is one that people of this culture would commonly use to mean that they were about to do something. If it would be helpful in your language, you could state the meaning plainly. Alternate translation: [I am about to create]

19.q: וְ⁠לֹֽא יִשָּׁמַ֥ע בָּ⁠הּ֙ ע֔וֹד ק֥וֹל בְּכִ֖י וְ⁠ק֥וֹל זְעָקָֽה
19.note: The expression **will no longer be heard** is a passive verbal form. If it would be unnatural to use that form, you could express the idea in active form or in another way that is natural in your language. Alternate translation: [and no longer will anyone hear the sound of weeping and the sound of an outcry in it]

20.note: Yahweh is using **An infant of days** as a common expression of the culture to mean an infant who lives for only a few days. If this phrase does not have that meaning for your readers, you could use a comparable expression from your language that does have that meaning, or you could state the meaning plainly. Alternate translation: [An infant who lives only a short time]

20.q: וְ⁠זָקֵ֔ן אֲשֶׁ֥ר לֹֽא יְמַלֵּ֖א אֶת יָמָ֑י⁠ו
20.note: Yahweh is leaving out some of the words that in many languages a sentence would need in order to be complete. You can supply these words from the context if that would be clearer in your language. Alternate translation: [or an elder who does not fill his days will no longer be from there]

20.q: וְ⁠זָקֵ֔ן אֲשֶׁ֥ר לֹֽא יְמַלֵּ֖א אֶת יָמָ֑י⁠ו
20.note: Yahweh is using **does not fill his days** as a common expression of the culture to mean that a person does not live out a complete lifespan. If this phrase does not have that meaning for your readers, you could use a comparable expression from your language that does have that meaning, or you could state the meaning plainly. Alternate translation: [or an elder who does not complete his lifespan] or [or an adult who does not lives as long as expected]

Yahweh is not referring to a specific **young man**. He means young men in general. If it would be helpful to your readers, you could use an expression that would be more natural in your language. Alternate translation: [young men will die]

Yahweh is using **a son of 100 years** as a common expression of the culture to mean a person who is 100 years old. If this phrase does not have that meaning for your readers, you could use a comparable expression from your language that does have that meaning, or you could state the meaning plainly. Alternate translation: [at the age of 100 years]

The expression **will be cursed** is a passive verbal form. If it would be unnatural to use that form, you could express the idea in active form or in another way that is natural in your language. Alternate translation: [people will considered that God has cursed]

22.note: Yahweh is using **their hands** to represent the people themselves as they work. If it would be helpful in your language, you could use an equivalent expression from your culture or state the meaning plainly. Alternate translation: [and my chosen ones will fully enjoy what they have made]

The point of this comparison is that just as **the days of a tree** are long, so **the days of** Yahweh’s **people** will be long. If it would be helpful in your language, you could make this point explicitly. Alternate translation: [the days of my people will be as long as the days of a tree]

23.note: If your language does not use an abstract noun for the idea of **worthlessness**, you could express the same idea in another way. Alternate translation: [They will not labor for what is worthless] or [They will not labor for what has no value]

The implication is that they will not give birth to children who are destined to experience sudden calamity. You could include this information if that would be helpful to your readers. Alternate translation: [and they will not give birth to children who will suffer sudden calamity]

If your language does not use an abstract noun for the idea of **terror**, you could express the same idea in another way. Alternate translation: [they will not birth children who will be suddenly terrified]

Here Yahweh is speaking of people’s descendants as if they were **seed** that those people produced. Your language may have a comparable expression that you can use in your translation, or you could state the meaning plainly. Alternate translation: [the descendants of the blessed of Yahweh]

The expression **the blessed of Yahweh** is a passive verbal form. If it would be unnatural to use that form, you could express the idea in active form or in another way that is natural in your language. Alternate translation: [the ones whom Yahweh has blessed]

Yahweh is leaving out some of the words that in many languages a sentence would need in order to be complete. You can supply these words from the context if that would be clearer in your language. Alternate translation: [and their offspring are blessed along with them]

24.note: Yahweh is stating the pronoun **I** separately, even though the verb translated as **I will answer** already includes this meaning. He is doing that to emphasize that he himself, and no one else, will be the one to respond to his people’s call. If a speaker of your language would use an explicit pronoun for the same purpose, you may want to use that construction in your translation. If not, your language may have other ways of showing the meaning here. Alternate translation: [that I myself will answer]

25.note: The point of this comparison is that just as **the ox** eats **straw** peacefully, so **the lion** will eat straw rather than hunting other animals. If it would be helpful in your language, you could make this point explicitly. Alternate translation: [and the lion will eat straw peacefully, just as the ox eats straw]

Yahweh is using **bread** to represent food in general. If it would be helpful in your language, you could use an equivalent expression from your culture or state the meaning plainly. Alternate translation: [dust will be its food]
